SNUGLITE (blind test): telemetry recovered from orbital physics

Every field below was found without a decoder: candidate byte readings were tested against sunlight, thermal lag, orbital phase, wall-clock time and the IGRF magnetic field computed from the TLE. Names, units and scales are Claude's reading of that evidence, with the satellite name withheld.

Frame type raw:len97

1005 frames, 126 passes, 97-byte payload

A 97-byte beacon with a large u4 counter, a GNSS block (ECEF position and velocity, 'no fix' frames read as -1), and a smooth u2 value that steps with sunlight, probably a battery voltage. The frame is mostly navigation data and is not a full housekeeping frame.

Health. Not much to go on in 16 days. The counter shows no resets, so there are no reboots. The battery voltage follows the sun-shadow cycle, with a daily low and high that do not drift, so there is no evidence of ageing. Thermal fields are not present.

battery_voltage [mV]

byte 59 · u2be · sun · power_battery
score 0.86 · ρ sun 0.864 · rough 0.085
raw * 1.0 · confidence 0.55

Smooth and narrow (spread 2%), in sun about 8294 versus 8158 in shadow, ratio 0.983. It falls in shadow (trend -0.64) and correlates with sun history (lag 5 min, rho 0.86). The 8.1-8.3k range fits a 2S Li-ion pack in mV.

Frame type raw:len214

405 frames, 108 passes, 214-byte payload

A 214-byte housekeeping/telemetry beacon with a GNSS position/velocity block (offsets 34-58), a block of sun-driven power values (offsets 59-87) and a block of temperature-like signed bytes (offsets 162-174), plus counters. All frames show an eclipse in the preceding 80 min, so lagged fields are real thermal or charge responses.

Health. No reboots are visible: the two slow counters at 27 and 160 never reset in the 15.8-day window. The temperatures swing with the lag expected of thermal inertia, and the voltage-like field at 59 follows sun and shadow. A mildly falling daily low in that field (about -15 raw per 30 days) is weak evidence of ageing over a short window, so overall health looks nominal with low confidence.
